cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the saints in Ephesus (Ephesians 1:1). He's just spent a whole stretch praising God for every spiritual blessing they have in Christ (Ephesians 1:3). Now he says, "For this reason," and tells them what he's heard about them.

cards.question: So what has Paul been hearing about the believers in Ephesus?

answers.text: Their faith in the Lord Jesus and their love for all the saints
Their courage in prison and their gifts to the poor in Jerusalem
Their bold preaching in the city and their care for widows

cards.text: Most of us hear good news about a friend, send ONE thumbs-up and get on with our day. But Paul has NOT STOPPED giving thanks for them, remembering them in his prayers.

cards.question: Paul prays that the glorious Father would give the Ephesian believers a spirit of wisdom and revelation in their ___ of Him.

cards.text: Then Paul asks that "the eyes of your heart may be enlightened". Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer with the lights off, so I am ALL for some eyes getting enlightened.

cards.question: When Paul asks for the eyes of their heart to be enlightened, he's praying for God to heal their eyesight.

cards.text: Paul wants their hearts to know "the hope of His calling, the riches of His glorious inheritance in the saints, and the surpassing greatness of His power to us who believe." Hope, riches AND power, friend: Paul does NOT pray small.
And how great is that power? Paul says it's in line with the working of God's mighty strength, the strength He exerted in Christ.

cards.question: Paul says God exerted His mighty strength in Christ. What did God do?

answers.text: He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand
He kept Him safe from every enemy He faced on the earth
He carried Him up to heaven in a chariot of fire

cards.question: Paul says God seated the risen Christ at His right hand in the heavenly realms.

cards.text: And that seat is "far above all rule and authority, power and dominion, and every name that is named". Regional manager, CEO, the guy whose email signature is four lines long: ALL of it is way, way down below.

cards.question: Paul says Christ is above every name, but only in this present age.

cards.text: Then Paul says God put everything under Christ's feet. Not most things, friend: EVERYTHING.

cards.question: God put everything under Christ's feet and made Him ___ over everything for the church.
Christ is head over everything for the church. So what does Paul call the church?

cards.text: Paul calls that body "the fullness of Him who fills all in all." He started with a thank-you for some friends in Ephesus and ended with Christ head over everything, friend, and I'm STILL trying to catch my breath.

findings.problem: This card is Ephesians 1:17 word for word with one word blanked out ('in your ___ of Him'). The baker hasn't seen this line yet, so they're guessing wording, not reasoning out meaning. 'Fear' is also a natural biblical pairing with wisdom (the fear of the Lord), so picking between 'knowledge' and 'fear' comes down to remembering the verse. Ask instead about what Paul is asking for, or why: for example, that God would give them wisdom and revelation so they know Him better.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card says 'how great is that power? Paul says it's in line with the working of God's mighty strength.' The BSB says 'These are in accordance with the working of His mighty strength' (Ephesians 1:19). 'These' is plural and points back to all three: the hope, the riches and the power. Tying it only to the power decides a connection the text leaves open. Keep it as 'these' or 'all of this.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question asks 'what does Paul call the church?' with no limit to this verse. Paul does call the church a holy temple (Ephesians 2:21) and pictures it as Christ's bride (Ephesians 5:25-32) in this same letter. A baker could argue that 'His bride' or 'His temple' is right. Either limit the question to this moment (for example, 'Right here, what does Paul call the church?') or replace those wrong answers with ones Paul never uses for the church.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
